subject: BTC debit nets into OPTION_PREMIUM at source level
statement: The BTC closing debit is emitted as a signed-negative PRODUCTION/OPTION_PREMIUM component, never CAPITAL_DEPLOYMENT (which was never summed) and never CAPITAL_EROSION (erosion is realized loss on disposition). There is no STO↔BTC matcher. Premium is still recognized once at STO (ADR-014). A missing closing debit gives UNRESOLVED.

subject: Temporal and per-event correctness for closes
statement: Summing all STO against all BTC cannot show an obligation existed when a BTC executed. Outstanding quantity is built from strictly prior events only. Same-day competing events fail closed, because date-only evidence cannot order intraday. Each BTC is its own dated chapter, so cross-month closes are not absorbed. Partial closes show the executed debit, not 'premium − debit' P&L.
verbatim: Same-day competing lifecycle events **fail closed** (date-only evidence cannot establish intraday order) rather than inventing a sequence.
speaker: Codex
notes: 'Quantity independent of cash' (j4:327): cash-known and quantity-known are independent facts.

subject: Unknown ≠ zero: uncertainty as a range; one lifecycle authority
statement: Recognized outstanding is an inclusive range [min,max]. Unknown prior consumption sets min to 0, and a close of q is deterministic only if min ≥ q. The frontend's competing resolver was removed: the backend OptionCloseResult is the single authority, and the Product renders it (divergence-guard test).
verbatim: **Retractions:** unknown prior consumption is NOT zero; accumulated episode opening quantity is NOT sufficient temporal evidence; backend and frontend do NOT independently run the same resolver (there is now one).

notes: Live-confirmed: STO 2 → unknown-qty BTC → BTC 2 gives outstandingBefore=[0,2], UNRESOLVED (j4:340).

subject: Covered ≠ complete; same-day ambiguity propagates; real round-trip
statement: DETERMINISTIC_COMPLETE requires residualMax == 0. A covered close leaving [0,2] is DETERMINISTIC_PARTIAL. An ambiguous prior event widens the range. The last frontend lifecycle authority, isFullyClosed(), was removed. Java-serialized ProductionResponse fixtures now drive the real frontend derivation, so divergence fails a test.
verbatim: "This close is covered" is not the same claim as "the obligation is completely retired."
